skills.title: Client email intake
skills.summary: Find the client and deal by the sender's email (on the CRM if your organisation has one, otherwise on Monday), save the attachments to the deal folder and register them on the deal.
skills.details: For the email you choose, the assistant finds the client and deal on your organisation's CRM by the sender's email address (if the organisation has no CRM, it finds the Deal on Monday), finds the deal folder (the folder the CRM has linked or will link to the deal, usually under Customers/; if there is none, it creates one with a tmp/ folder), saves the attachments that aren't there yet into tmp/ to be checked later, then registers those files on the deal on the CRM. If there is no client or deal yet, the assistant proposes creating them and only creates them when you agree. Asking it to process an email covers creating the folder, saving the files and registering them, in Ask first and Full access mode; in Plan only mode it only says what it would do. The assistant doesn't rename files, change Monday or reply to the email; files stay in tmp/ until they are checked and you approve filing.
examples: Process this email and save the files to the deal
Save the documents the client sent in this email to the deal

skills.title: Check loan documents
skills.summary: Check a client's documents against the 23-item checklist and report what needs doing; with the CRM it also shows which clients have sent new documents, processes a deal's new files and files them when you approve.
skills.details: The assistant checks the source file (genuine issued copy, edited, photo or scan), recognises the document type, reads it by that type's rules and cross-checks the documents. The report gives the conclusion, the details for the Fact Find and what to tell the client. When your organisation has the CRM, the assistant lists the deals with files clients sent through the client portal that are still waiting (new files, and files registered but not checked yet) for you to choose from, then processes each deal's new files one deal at a time (files sent through the client portal, plus other files in the deal's tmp/ such as files saved from email): registers them on the deal, recognises the document type and client, links them to required documents, and records the results on the deal (suggested values, items to tell the client, whether each criterion is met). Satisfied documents (all criteria met, or ticked or accepted by you) are proposed for filing: the assistant shows the name the naming rule suggests and the target folder, you keep the name or give your own, and the CRM only renames and moves the files you agree to in Ask first mode, or the files you asked it to file in Full access mode. For a document with open items you decide, in one answer: accept it as it is with your reason (and file it, or accept only), tick specific criteria, request a new one or leave it. When you ask, the assistant renames a filed file. If the deal has no owner, the assistant reminds you to claim the deal; it doesn't claim it itself. For a returning client whose deal has no folder, the assistant looks for the client's old folder on OneDrive, proposes attaching it to the deal (keeping the folder name) and only attaches it when you confirm. When you ask, the assistant moves the client portal account of a client who activated the client portal themselves to an existing contact (owners or admins only), after you point to the right contact and agree. The assistant doesn't copy TFNs, Medicare numbers or card numbers, and never renames or moves files on its own.
examples: Has any client sent new documents?
Process the files clients just sent
Process the new files the client sent in the Whitmore deal's tmp
Check the documents in client Nguyễn Văn A's folder
Check the payslip and statement I just attached
Is this tax return the original downloaded from myGov?

skills.title: Australian business lookup (ABN)
skills.summary: Look up an ABN, ACN or business name: active or cancelled, GST, and whether it matches the name on the document.
skills.details: The assistant looks up the business on the Australian Business Register's ABN Lookup, gives the entity name, entity type, ABN status (active or cancelled, and since when), GST and business names, then lists what needs action: a cancelled ABN, a wrong ABN number, or a business name that differs from the document (allowing for trust names and sole traders' names). A printout or screenshot of an ABN Lookup result sent by the client is looked up again, not used as evidence. Registration status with ASIC (whether a company has been deregistered) isn't in the ABR, so the assistant says clearly that it couldn't check it. The assistant never guesses business details from memory.
examples: Is ABC Pty Ltd still active?
